header.stance: 買回期待退潮，高殖利率仍吸引標售需求

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## $60億買回方案不如期待，美債下跌

燃料價格上升，財政部擴大買回的規模又低於市場最積極的預期，美債因而下跌。10年期殖利率一度升至4.85%，收盤上升3個基點至4.83%；2年期上升4個基點至4.43%，30年期上升3個基點至5.28%。10年期標售吸引買方進場，但仍不足以收復全天跌幅。

財政部將下一次10至20年期買回操作上限定為$60億，是原先$20億的三倍，卻低於部分人士最高$100億的估計。上午油價與聯準會升息預期先壓低短端價格，公告後則轉為長端領跌。全日曲線仍小幅趨平，2年與10年期利差收窄1個基點至40個基點。

與週二不同，10年期殖利率的漲幅全數來自實質殖利率，上升3個基點至2.46%，損益兩平通膨率維持2.37%。布蘭特原油升至$102.05，歐洲柴油溢價也急速擴大。更多貨幣緊縮的可能性，加上官方買盤不如部分預期，使投資人要求更高的實質報酬。

企業融資仍活絡。美國投資級利差明顯收窄，強勢貨幣新興債小幅收窄，高收益卻小幅擴大。Dell擴大美元發行，Amazon與Uber完成海外首發，MercadoLibre重返國際債。訂單反映成長與再融資需求，也顯示持續增加長天期曝險的胃納較有限。信用成交強，未讓政府長債免於資金競爭。

## 買回期待退潮後，高標售殖利率吸引買方

這次$60億指的是買回債券的面額上限，並非承諾支出同額現金；若折價買入，實際支出會小於註銷本金。截至11月5日，其餘六次涵蓋10至20年及20至30年期名目債的操作，個別上限仍訂為至少$40億，而非每次都承諾$60億。週三公布的是後續操作安排，買回尚未執行。

Natixis的John Briggs指出，赤字與科技資本支出仍持續需要資金。買回流動性較差的舊券，可以讓投資人騰出部位承接新券，卻不會消除政府與企業之間的資金競爭。規模確定後，市場反而回吐先前押注更大干預所帶來的漲幅。

下午1點，財政部續發8月首次發行$420億的10年期券，本次規模$390億，得標殖利率4.834%，創2007年以來最高。雖然絕對殖利率高，結果仍比標售前市場水準低約1.5個基點，顯示買方願意承接，也幫助價格回穩。德國同日以3.39%發行€42億2036年8月到期債，10年期標售殖利率也創17年新高。

高利率已影響房貸需求。MBA截至9月4日當週的30年期房貸契約利率，由6.79%上升6個基點至6.85%，創逾一年最高；申請量則由前週增加0.8%轉為減少2.7%。轉貸申請下降6.2%，指數由732.6降至687.3，創2025年5月以來最低；購屋申請僅減少0.2%，指數由157.8降至157.5。五年期機動利率房貸則逆勢下降至6.13%。

轉貸減少會延長房貸投資人的存續期間，可能促使賣債或在交換支付固定利率。選擇權交易商也有類似壓力：客戶買防殖利率上升的保護，對手方可能須賣期貨或支付固定來避險。一筆近期大部位針對30年約5.7%的不利情境，不是預測必然到達。Morgan Stanley的Shaun Zhou指出，房貸及選擇權是兩群不同的大型投資人，都可能放大變動。

投資人部位並非全面偏空。摩根大通截至9月8日當週的客戶調查顯示，空頭占比減少6個百分點，資金轉向中性部位，使淨多頭升至11月以來最高，並非全由新增多頭推動。長端期貨選擇權仍顯示，防範債價下跌的保護較昂貴，短端與中段則接近中性。

ADP每週新增就業為1.2萬人，前值修正為1萬人；Redbook截至9月5日當週的銷售年增率，則由9.6%降至8.3%。市場反映的聯準會升息機率由週二60%升至約62%，明年中前至少兩次升息已完全計入。國內需求的訊號仍有分歧：房市受到壓抑，就業卻小幅改善。

聯準會的溝通安排也有討論。六名地區聯準銀行總裁願意考慮Kevin Warsh的提議，將每年八次例行決策減為六次，另兩次改作深入經濟討論，包括Beth Hammack、Jeffrey Schmid與Anna Paulson。Paulson要求完整評估，Austan Goolsbee則支持更廣泛檢討溝通方式。方案尚未定案，討論的是資訊與預測如何安排，不能視為短期升息立場的轉變。

## 柴油讓通膨問題超出原油本身

布蘭特原油升至$102.05，WTI為$97.01。伊朗試圖以彈道飛彈攻擊美國軍艦後，美方摧毀五艘伊朗油輪；中央司令部表示，軍艦未受損並繼續巡邏。加上先前攻擊，數日內被摧毀的油輪共八艘。中國暫停採購後也恢復購油。TD的Ryan McKay表示，非正式運輸量增加曾緩解供應缺口，但面對新攻擊與需求回升，市場仍然吃緊。

歐洲柴油相對布蘭特原油的溢價，已由1月2日每桶$21擴大至約$75，使批發價格接近$175。加上稅負與業者利潤，歐洲加油站的汽柴油價格換算每桶超過$370。煉油廠受損與出口限制，使原油供應增加也未必能降低可用燃料的成本；俄羅斯煉廠遭襲、柴油出口禁令延長，又加重壓力。

成品油通過荷姆茲海峽所需船隻比原油更多，也缺乏主導貨主協調通行。Vitol的Russell Hardy週二估計，中東每日減少約200萬桶成品油出口，俄羅斯則因烏克蘭無人機攻擊再減少200萬桶。這些加工與運輸限制推高裂解價差，也是Bailey關注的問題：即使原油穩定，柴油與運輸成本仍可能居高不下。

交換市場反映，截至2027年12月歐洲央行將升息約90個基點，為本輪最高，英國定價也大致相同。德國2年期殖利率升至3.08%，創2024年6月以來新高。Allspring的Lauren van Biljon認為，能源與經濟韌性支持歐洲的升息預期，卻較不認同英國路徑。CG的Emma Moriarty也認為，英國經濟疲弱，要出現足以迫使央行升息多達四次的衝擊，可能性不高。

波蘭連續第六個月維持利率3.75%，符合34名經濟學家全數預期，茲羅提變動不大。通膨3.4%創14個月新高，接近2.5%目標的容許上緣，加上成長較強、燃油限價到期，使先前9月降息的期待消退。後續預測仍分歧：Pekao估利率維持至明年底；Pocztowy的Monika Kurtek認為2027年下半年可能降息；Credit Agricole的Jakub Borowski則預估2026年第4季升息25個基點。

智利央行在季度報告中，第三度下修今年成長預測，由1%至1.75%降為0.25%至0.75%，2027年仍維持2%至3%。政策利率目前4.5%，通膨4.1%。儘管投資前景仍佳，經濟疲弱延續，使央行若為抑制進口物價而緊縮，必須承擔更大的成長代價。

墨西哥整體通膨由3.12%升至3.26%，低於3.30%預估；核心通膨由3.95%降至3.88%，低於3.92%預期，兩者都在3%目標上下1個百分點的範圍內。能源補貼、先前披索升值與閒置產能，緩衝了成本上漲；服務價格及勞動市場壓力，則限制政策利率從6.5%繼續下調的空間。

丹麥六名受訪分析師全數預期，未來至少12個月仍會跟隨歐洲央行調整利率，儘管克朗承壓。目前利率1.85%，低於歐洲央行40個基點，丹麥央行已在6月與8月買入合計DKK63億克朗。AL Sydbank的Soren Kristensen估計，干預至少達DKK200億才可能考慮獨立升息，其他分析師則估接近DKK500億；這些並非官方門檻，股利支付也可能解釋部分暫時性匯率壓力。

華府準備加碼回應加拿大反制，措施包括阻擋部分進口、其中有某些黑麥威士忌，增加關稅，並尋求限制加拿大企業向美國政府承包商銷售。這將增加美國進口成本，也擴大加拿大企業的市場風險。中國消費通膨則自4月以來首次加速，出廠價格漲幅也超出預期，顯示價格壓力並不限於歐美。

## Dell、Amazon與Uber完成大型發債，需求各有差異

16家美國投資級借款人募集$230億，加上週二18家，為1月5至6日以來最多兩日家數，與美債標售同時爭取資金。

Dell將發行規模由原估$40億提高至$50億，分為四檔，天期由三年至10年。最高訂單約$230億，接近發行額五倍，高於今年投資級平均約四倍；最長券定價較美債高110個基點，比初步討論最多收窄30個基點。資金將用於今年到期債務及一般企業用途，也可能償還其他債務，其中10月有$23億到期。Smith & Nephew、Blue Owl Credit Income與Rogers Communications也在進行再融資。

Dell上調AI伺服器展望，並將財年營收預測提高$250億，支持投資人需求。除Nvidia相關設備外，以CPU管理AI代理的需求也有利傳統設備。Bloomberg Intelligence的Robert Schiffman認為，公司能在再融資、增加股東分配的同時，維持BBB區間中段的信用水準。

Amazon首次發行英鎊債，四檔共募集£42.5億。發行規模雖然增加，訂單卻由高峰逾£120億降至£106.5億。三年期定價較英債高53個基點，19年期高93個基點，後者需求最少；2032年到期券的訂單比Alphabet相近天期少£14億，最終利差也較寬。整筆交易仍能較初步指引收窄，但投資人明顯區分發行人與天期。加上此前歐元、瑞郎及加幣融資，Amazon今年籌資已接近$1,000億等值。

Uber募集€45億，分為五檔固定利率債，天期由三年至20年。最終訂單超過€150億，高峰曾超過€210億，最短與最長券分別較交換利率高45及170個基點。惠譽評為A−，看重Delivery Hero帶來的地域與規模效益，穆迪及標普則給予相當於BBB+的評等。先前的銀行委任已轉為完成發行，也讓融資幣別與歐洲業務相連。

Amazon與Uber名列當日六家赴歐發債的美國企業，家數創紀錄。這些交易之前，美國企業今年已在歐洲募集€1,490億，僅次於2025年全年紀錄。有歐元收入的公司可直接受惠於較低利息，但若透過遠期交易換回美元，近期成本與直接發行美元債大致相同。歐洲本地企業供給也多，美國企業占歐元投資級市場的比重，較2025年初增加不到1個百分點。

MercadoLibre發行$10億2036年到期債，定價較美債高130個基點，為第三次國際發債、去年12月以來首次。既有2033年券利差約100個基點，但天期較短，不能直接把兩者差額當成新券讓利。惠譽與標普評為BBB−，穆迪為Baa3。公司第2季營收增加50%至$102億，已連續30季成長逾30%；穆迪仍警告，物流與Mercado Pago投資會壓低獲利，並增加融資及資產品質風險。

Barclays主導的銀行團準備€24億融資，支持Lone Star收購ContiTech，預計包含€19億等值美元與歐元貸款，以及€5億高收益債。這筆€40億收購將讓Continental取得約€31億現金，另有最高€2.5億績效款；公司計畫減債並向股東分配約€25億。ContiTech的融資價格則尚未確定。

墨西哥Kapital透過股權與債務募集$1.25億，由Tru Arrow主導，Fasanara提供放貸資金。公司上半年淨利$5,000萬，貸款增加220%、存款增加234%，快速擴張使風險管理更重要。資產交易方面，Dow考慮出售其持有的Sadara 35%股權，這是與Aramco合資的$200億項目；Enbridge則深入協商以約$20億收購Tallgrass的Pony Express管線。兩案均未完成，也尚未宣布債務融資安排。

## 日圓強促使替代融資與離岸人民幣需求

即使美債殖利率上升，美元指數仍下跌0.0577%至98.783，日圓則升值。Bessent週二晚間對日圓空頭的警告持續影響交易，但前日本央行首席經濟學家Seisaku Kameda認為，部分投資人預期升息50個基點或連續升息，可能過度積極。日圓轉強本身會壓低進口通膨，反而可能減少快速升息的必要性。

JPMorgan的Rie Nishihara認為，強日圓可減輕日債殖利率壓力、有利AI、半導體及地產，卻傷運輸、物流與汽車；Saxo的Charu Chanana重視槓桿部位撤回。進口成本減少與日圓融資的海外部位虧損可並存。

以離岸人民幣借款、買入八種新興市場貨幣組合的策略，三個月報酬率為1.5%，同期日圓融資策略虧損1%。較低且穩定的利率，以及受管理的匯率，吸引投資人考慮人民幣融資。法國興業銀行的Kiyong Seong認為，目前人民幣升值風險與利差收益大致抵銷，若利差擴大，報酬可能改善；但人民幣尚未完全自由兌換，長天期借款市場也較淺，限制了交易規模。

DTCC資料顯示，9月前八天，美元兌離岸人民幣賣權的日均交易量比8月增加逾60%，並超過買權。這類部位可用來防範人民幣升值，與融資需求相符，但交易量不等於已建立的套利部位。中國央行支持人民幣用於國際債券、貸款及貿易融資，卻無意鼓勵單向放空人民幣。

知情人士表示，規模約$5,680億的全國社保基金，可能獲准透過南向債券通投資，無須另行申請海外額度；理事會正透過外部經理人準備點心債投資計畫。截至2025年底，基金海外資產為CN¥5,800億、約$864億，占15.23%。新安排可能拓寬投資管道，但尚未公布購買金額。

境外人民幣債有較高收益的誘因。國家電網上月10年期點心債票息2.18%，比一週後同天期境內發行高約20個基點。估計7月內地資金透過南向管道淨買入CN¥496億，為連續第14個月流入，也是六個月最大。點心債供給約CN¥8,300億，年增逾30%。

Vale財務長Marcelo Bacci表示，公司正準備可能的首次中國境內發債，中國約占其營收50%。當地國際發行人的典型規模為$4億至$5億，天期多為兩年、三年或五年，Vale則希望探索更長天期，尚未宣布規模。公司已有足夠資金支持成長，未來一至兩年不急於讓基本金屬業務上市；若之後出現合適的銅投資機會，仍可能重新考慮。

歐洲央行擔保品規則也將改變融資價值。央行已採用反映氣候轉型風險的調整因子，預計2027年底由公司債擴及貸款債權；後者接近擔保品的30%，可能再被扣減最多5%的價值。銀行業團體質疑發行人揭露不足，BBVA也表示自有模型結果可能明顯不同。目前央行再融資規模僅€260億，相較€1.59兆擔保品，整體壓力有限；若未來借款需求提高，高曝險貸款能取得的融資就會減少。實體氣候風險仍屬未來可能納入的項目，不在目前計算之內。

## Pemex支持減少，Dangote還債，SoftBank換下過橋貸款

墨西哥明年將編列MXN810億、約$48億，協助Pemex償債，援助比先前減少近70%。政府預估公司在移轉支付前可有MXN140億盈餘，2027年則約有$50億債務到期。Claudia Sheinbaum重申，公司自身財務可支持發展，但Edgar Amador並未說明何時停止援助；預算減少尚不代表政府後盾終止。

社福與建設支出增加，使墨西哥赤字僅由GDP的4.1%改善至3.9%。Pemex預算增加2%至MXN5,270億，建設支出接近四倍、達近MXN2,360億，預估原油及凝析油日產量180萬桶，比目前增加約6%。九個專案已與民間達成正式協議，但老油田、煉油業務過往虧損，以及願意參與的大型伙伴有限，仍使減少政府移轉支付有賴營運改善；Petrobras是少數表達興趣的企業之一。

Dangote煉油廠的有擔保債務，由去年底$62.4億降至6月底$56.7億，已償還$5.7億。戰時市場條件及產銷增加，使上半年由前期虧損$2.821億，轉為獲利$18.2億；淨債務降至EBITDA的0.27倍。

公司擬發行41億股，每股NGN525、約$0.40，募集$16億，並可視需求及核准情況增至$21億。目前煉油廠每日處理70萬桶，另規劃投入$143億，在2030年將產能倍增，並非全數資金都須立即到位。Aliko Dangote間接持股87.3%；已完成的還款、擬議股權籌資與較晚的擴建支出，仍須分別看待。

SoftBank宣布將償還原本用於OpenAI投資及其他成本的$400億過橋貸款，剩餘餘額為$259億。這筆無擔保美元貸款原定明年3月到期，公司正安排長期債券、銀行貸款及資產擔保融資替代。近期以OpenAI股份支持的$100億保證金貸款，也改變了債權保障結構；提前償還過橋貸款，並不等於合併槓桿已下降。

Huachen Energy尋求第二次展延，擬將美元及人民幣債務再延六年，首年利率6%，之後每年增加0.5個百分點，第六年達8.5%。若償還指定本金，可減少利息，但年度攤還安排仍有爭議。前次法院批准展延五年至2026年12月，目前美元債餘額約$6.27億；境內CN¥20億則是2021年重整時的金額，並非目前總債務。中金公司正擔任美元債協商顧問。

LIV Golf週二聲請破產後，先前退出融資的沙烏地PIF同意提供$4,960萬債務人持有資產融資，支持破產程序。這項承諾不代表恢復原先資助模式，既有債權人的回收結果也尚未確定。

## 通膨與首次擴大買回提供下一輪證據

市場預估9月10日PPI整體月增0.4%、核心月增0.3%，初領失業救濟金人數為20.5萬人，前期20.6萬人；9月11日CPI預估月增0.4%、核心月增0.2%，核心年增率由2.5%降至2.4%。若非能源價格加速，將支持9月16日聯準會採取行動；若持續降溫，房市受到的抑制就更值得權衡。9月10日歐洲央行的後續指引，則將檢驗截至2027年底約90個基點的升息定價，而不只決定當次利率。

9月10日將進行上限$60億的買回操作，同日還有30年期標售。週三10年期需求強勁之後，實際買回量與流動性變化，將顯示官方支持能否減輕賣壓；若需求良好、價格卻仍疲弱，房貸與選擇權避險的影響就更值得關注。SoftBank宣布9月15日償還過橋貸款，則是另一項待落實的現金支付。

市場已反映日本央行9月18日升息25個基點，日圓後續走勢更取決於指引。升息步調若慢於預期，可能回吐部分升值；若確認更積極的路徑，則可能加速日圓融資部位調整。與此同時，日圓轉強本身也有助緩解進口通膨。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Treasuries fall as $6 billion buyback plan disappoints

Treasuries sold off as fuel prices climbed and the government's enlarged buyback fell short of the most ambitious market expectations. The 10-year yield closed 3 basis points higher at 4.83% after touching 4.85%; the 2-year rose 4 to 4.43% and the 30-year 3 to 5.28%. A well-received 10-year auction brought buyers back but did not erase the decline.

Treasury set a $6 billion maximum for the next 10- to 20-year operation, triple the original $2 billion but below estimates as high as $10 billion. Long maturities led selling after the announcement, following earlier front-end pressure from oil and Fed expectations. The full-day curve still flattened modestly, with 2s10s down 1 basis point to 40.

Unlike Tuesday, the 10-year move came through real yields, up 3 basis points to 2.46%, while breakevens stayed at 2.37%. Brent reached $102.05 and European diesel premiums widened sharply. Investors raised the real return required to lend as markets contemplated more monetary restraint and less official support than some had anticipated.

Corporate financing remained active. US IG spreads tightened noticeably, hard-currency EM modestly, while HY widened modestly. Dell enlarged its dollar sale, Amazon and Uber completed overseas debuts, and MercadoLibre returned to international bonds. Their orderbooks showed demand for growth and refinancing, but also less appetite for repeated long-dated exposure. Strong credit placement did not spare government duration from the competition for funds.

## High auction yields attract buyers after buyback expectations unwind

The $6 billion buyback is a face-value ceiling, not a cash-spending pledge: buying bonds below par costs less than the principal retired. The other six long-dated nominal operations through November 5, covering 10–20 and 20–30 years, retain maximums of at least $4 billion. Treasury did not promise repeated $6 billion purchases, and no buyback had yet been completed Wednesday.

Natixis's John Briggs pointed to deficits and technology capex as underlying demands for cash. Buying less-liquid old bonds can free balance-sheet capacity for new issues, but the announcement could not remove those competing needs. Clarifying the amount instead unwound some support that speculation about a larger intervention had provided.

At 1 p.m., Treasury reopened August's $42 billion issue with $39 billion of 10-year notes at 4.834%, the highest auction yield since 2007. The result was about 1.5 basis points through the pre-auction market, helping prices recover. Buyers accepted the reopening readily at a historically high funding cost. Germany likewise sold €4.2 billion of August 2036 debt at 3.39%, its highest 10-year auction yield in 17 years.

Higher yields were already reaching mortgages. MBA's 30-year contract rate rose 6 basis points to 6.85% in the week through September 4, highest in over a year, from 6.79%. Applications fell 2.7% after +0.8%. Refinancing dropped 6.2% to the lowest since May 2025, with its index at 687.3 from 732.6; purchases fell just 0.2%, to 157.5 from 157.8. Five-year adjustable rates instead declined to 6.13%.

Slower refinancing extends mortgage duration. Investors may sell bonds or pay fixed in swaps to offset it, adding pressure as yields rise. Options dealers face a parallel need when clients buy protection against higher yields: hedging can require futures selling or fixed-rate paying. One large recent position targeted a 30-year yield around 5.7%, an adverse-outcome hedge rather than a forecast. Morgan Stanley's Shaun Zhou identified mortgage and options investors as separate large groups capable of amplifying a move.

Positioning was not uniformly bearish. JPMorgan's client survey showed shorts falling 6 percentage points in the week through September 8 as investors moved to neutral. Net longs reached their highest since November without necessarily adding outright bullish positions. Long-end futures options still priced more downside protection, while front and belly were near neutral.

Weekly ADP hiring was 12,000 versus a revised 10,000, while Redbook annual sales growth slowed to 8.3% from 9.6% through September 5. Fed hike odds reached about 62% from Tuesday's 60%, with at least two increases fully priced by mid-next year. Housing restraint and modest hiring improvement kept the domestic picture more mixed than fuel prices.

Separately, six regional Fed presidents expressed openness to Kevin Warsh's proposal for six regular rate meetings rather than eight, reserving two for substantive economic discussion. Beth Hammack, Jeffrey Schmid and Anna Paulson were among them; Paulson wanted fuller evaluation, and Austan Goolsbee favored reconsidering communications more broadly. The undecided proposal concerns information and projection cadence, not a new near-term hawkish coalition.

## Diesel costs extend the inflation problem beyond crude

Brent reached $102.05 and WTI $97.01. The US destroyed five Iranian tankers following attempted ballistic-missile attacks on a Navy vessel; Central Command said the ship was unharmed and continued patrol. Eight tankers destroyed over several days includes earlier attacks, not eight more. Chinese crude buying also resumed after a pause. TD's Ryan McKay said greater unofficial flows had eased the deficit, but the market remained tight before the renewed attacks and demand.

European diesel traded around $75 a barrel above Brent, versus $21 on January 2, implying wholesale fuel near $175. Taxes and margins put European pump-price equivalents for gasoline and diesel above $370 a barrel. Refinery damage and product-export restrictions mean more crude cannot fully relieve usable-fuel costs. Attacks on Russian refineries and an extended Russian diesel-export ban tightened supply further.

Products require more individual vessels through Hormuz than crude and lack a dominant shipper organizing transit. Vitol's Russell Hardy estimated Tuesday that the Middle East had lost about 2 million barrels a day of product exports and Russia another 2 million after Ukrainian drone attacks. Those losses help explain the premium and Bailey's focus on crack spreads: transport costs may stay elevated even if crude steadies.

Swaps priced roughly 90 basis points of ECB hikes through December 2027, the most this cycle, and around the same for the BOE. German 2-year yields reached 3.08%, highest since June 2024. Allspring's Lauren van Biljon linked ECB repricing to energy and greater economic resilience but was less persuaded by the British path. CG Asset Management's Emma Moriarty considered a shock requiring as many as four UK hikes unlikely given weak activity.

Poland held 3.75% for a sixth month, as all 34 economists expected, with the zloty little changed. Inflation of 3.4%, a 14-month high near the tolerance ceiling around the 2.5% target, stronger growth and expiring fuel caps had displaced September cut expectations. Subsequent forecasts diverge: Pekao sees a hold through next year, Pocztowy's Monika Kurtek possible easing in the second half of 2027, and Credit Agricole's Jakub Borowski a quarter-point Q4 2026 hike.

Chile's quarterly report cut this year's growth range to 0.25%–0.75% from 1%–1.75%, its third downgrade, leaving 2027 at 2%–3%. With policy already at 4.5% and inflation 4.1%, longer weakness increases the cost of responding to imported prices with restraint, despite a favorable investment assessment.

Mexico's headline inflation rose to 3.26% from 3.12% but missed 3.30% consensus; core slowed to 3.88% from 3.95%, below 3.92% forecast. Both remain within the 3% target's 1-percentage-point band. Energy subsidies, prior peso strength and slack cushion costs, while services and labor limit easing room at the 6.5% policy rate.

All six economists surveyed expect Denmark to match the ECB for at least 12 months despite krone pressure. The 1.85% rate is 40 basis points below the ECB's; Nationalbanken bought DKK6.3 billion in June and August. AL Sydbank's Soren Kristensen saw intervention needing at least DKK20 billion before an independent hike, others nearer DKK50 billion. These are analyst estimates, not official triggers; dividends may explain some temporary pressure.

Washington escalated its response to Canadian retaliation, moving to block some imports including certain rye whiskies, add tariffs and seek restrictions on Canadian firms selling to government contractors. This adds US import costs and Canadian market-access risk. China's consumer inflation accelerated for the first time since April and factory-gate prices rose faster than expected, broadening the geographical pressure without a supplied numerical surprise.

## Dell, Amazon and Uber complete large sales with different demand

Sixteen US IG borrowers raised $23 billion. Combined with Tuesday's 18, it was the largest two-day issuer count since January 5–6, adding corporate funding alongside the Treasury auction.

Dell raised $5 billion versus $4 billion initially expected, in four tranches from three to 10 years. Peak orders near $23 billion were almost five times the deal, versus this year's roughly four-times IG average. The longest tranche priced 110 basis points over Treasuries, up to 30 tighter than initial discussion. Proceeds refinance this year's maturities and general needs, potentially other debt; $2.3 billion matures in October. Smith & Nephew, Blue Owl Credit Income and Rogers Communications also refinanced.

Dell's AI-server growth and $25 billion increase in its fiscal-year sales forecast supported demand. Its Nvidia-equipped and traditional machines also benefit as CPUs manage AI agents. Bloomberg Intelligence's Robert Schiffman judged it able to refinance and increase shareholder distributions while retaining a mid-BBB profile.

Amazon completed a £4.25 billion sterling debut in four tranches, enlarging the sale even as orders fell from over £12 billion to £10.65 billion. Three-year debt priced 53 basis points over gilts; the 19-year at 93 attracted least demand. Its 2032 tranche drew £1.4 billion fewer orders and priced wider than Alphabet's comparable maturity. Terms still tightened in execution, but buyers differentiated issuer and maturity. Amazon's 2026 issuance now approaches $100 billion-equivalent after earlier euro, Swiss-franc and Canadian-dollar borrowing.

Uber raised €4.5 billion across five fixed-rate tranches, three to 20 years. Final orders exceeded €15 billion, versus a peak above €21 billion. The ends priced at mid-swaps plus 45 and 170 basis points. Fitch assigned A-, citing Delivery Hero's geographic diversification and scale, while Moody's and S&P assigned BBB+ equivalents. The completed financing follows the earlier mandate and connects the currency to European expansion.

They were among an unprecedented six US issuers in Europe that day. Even before these deals, US companies had raised €149 billion in European markets this year, second only to the 2025 annual record. Euro revenues can support lower service costs, but converting proceeds to dollars through forwards had recently cost about the same as direct dollar borrowing. European issuance also remains heavy: the US share of euro IG is less than 1 percentage point above early 2025.

MercadoLibre sold $1 billion of 2036 notes at Treasury plus 130 basis points, its third international offering and first since December. Existing 2033 debt around 100 is a shorter-maturity reference, not a direct concession measure. New ratings are BBB- at Fitch/S&P and Baa3 at Moody's. Q2 revenue grew 50% to $10.2 billion, the 30th quarter above 30%, while logistics and Mercado Pago investment depress profitability and add funding/asset-quality risk, Moody's warned.

Barclays-led banks are preparing €2.4 billion for Lone Star's ContiTech purchase: an expected €1.9 billion dollar/euro term loan and €500 million HY bond. The €4 billion acquisition would give Continental about €3.1 billion cash plus a performance-linked element up to €250 million. It plans debt reduction and roughly €2.5 billion shareholder distributions; the acquired business's financing price remains unset.

Mexico's Kapital raised $125 million in combined debt/equity, led by Tru Arrow with Fasanara lending finance. First-half net income was $50 million, loans up 220% and deposits 234%, making risk controls important as expansion accelerates. Dow is considering selling its 35% stake in the $20 billion Sadara venture with Aramco; Enbridge is in advanced talks for Tallgrass's Pony Express pipeline at about $2 billion. Neither asset transaction is complete or an announced debt financing.

## Yen strength encourages alternative funding and offshore yuan access

DXY closed 0.0577% lower at 98.783 despite higher Treasury yields, while the yen advanced. Bessent's Tuesday-evening challenge to yen bears still influenced trading. Former BOJ chief economist Seisaku Kameda thought some expectations for 50 basis points or consecutive hikes excessive. Yen appreciation itself can reduce imported inflation and soften the case for the faster policy path supporting it.

JPMorgan's Rie Nishihara saw a stronger currency relieving JGB yield pressure and helping AI, semiconductor and property shares while hurting transport, logistics and autos. Saxo's Charu Chanana emphasized leveraged-position unwinds. Lower domestic import costs and losses on yen-funded foreign positions can occur together.

Offshore-yuan funding returned 1.5% over three months against a basket of eight EM currencies, versus a 1% loss for yen funding. Low stable Chinese rates and managed FX attract interest. Societe Generale's Kiyong Seong judged appreciation risk versus carry broadly balanced now, with wider rate differentials potentially improving returns. Limited convertibility and thinner long-dated borrowing constrain scale.

DTCC showed daily dollar-offshore-yuan put volumes up over 60% in September's first eight days versus August, outpacing calls. Hedging yuan appreciation fits funding interest but does not measure established carry positions. PBOC support for international bonds, loans and trade finance coexists with little incentive to encourage one-way yuan selling.

People familiar said the $568 billion National Social Security Fund could gain Southbound Bond Connect access without applying for overseas quotas; its council was preparing dim sum plans through external managers. Fund size is not a purchase commitment. End-2025 overseas holdings were CN¥580 billion/$86.4 billion, or 15.23% of assets.

The yield incentive is visible: State Grid's 10-year dim sum coupon was 2.18% last month, roughly 20 basis points above its onshore issue a week later. Mainland institutions added an estimated CN¥49.6 billion through Southbound in July, the 14th net-inflow month and largest in six. Dim sum supply reached about CN¥830 billion, over 30% higher annually.

Vale CFO Marcelo Bacci said it was preparing a possible onshore debut, with China providing about 50% of revenue. Typical international issues there are $400 million–$500 million at two, three or five years; Vale is exploring longer borrowing, not announcing that size. A base-metals IPO is not a priority for one to two years given available growth capital, though later copper opportunities could justify it.

European collateral rules will separately change some assets' funding value. The ECB extends its adopted transition-risk climate factor from corporate bonds to credit claims, nearly 30% of pledged collateral, at end-2027, allowing up to 5% additional haircut. The banking federation and others challenge missing issuer-level disclosure; BBVA says its own model may differ materially. Refinancing is only about €26 billion against €1.59 trillion collateral, limiting immediate aggregate strain. Exposed loans could nevertheless support less borrowing when liquidity needs rise. Physical climate risk is a possible later extension, not part of this calculation.

## Pemex support falls as Dangote repays and SoftBank replaces its bridge

Mexico earmarks MXN81 billion/$4.8 billion for Pemex debt payments next year, nearly 70% less aid, and projects a pre-transfer MXN14 billion surplus. About $5 billion matures in 2027. Claudia Sheinbaum reiterated that Pemex's finances would sustain development, while Edgar Amador declined to specify when aid could end. The budget cuts support without announcing a definitive end to the backstop.

Mexico's deficit improves only to 3.9% of GDP from 4.1% as social and infrastructure spending rises. Pemex's budget grows 2% to MXN527 billion; infrastructure nearly quadruples to almost MXN236 billion. Crude and condensate are projected near 1.8 million barrels daily, about 6% above current output, with private agreements formalized for nine projects. Lower transfers depend on stronger operations despite aging fields, historically loss-making refining and limited major-partner interest; Petrobras is among the few expressing interest.

Dangote's refinery has already reduced secured debt by $570 million, to $5.67 billion at June-end from $6.24 billion. First-half profit of $1.82 billion reversed a $282.1 million loss as output and sales rose, helped by wartime conditions. Net debt was 0.27 times EBITDA.

Its planned share sale seeks $1.6 billion through 4.1 billion shares at NGN525/$0.40, potentially $2.1 billion subject to demand and approval. Processing 700,000 barrels daily, it plans $14.3 billion to double capacity by 2030, explicitly not an immediate funding need. Aliko Dangote indirectly owns 87.3%. Current repayment and a prospective equity sale are distinct from that later capex.

SoftBank announced it would repay the $25.9 billion remaining on its $40 billion OpenAI-and-other-costs bridge, an unsecured dollar facility otherwise due next March. This fixes an early takeout amount while permanent bonds, bank and asset-backed financing develop. A recently secured $10 billion OpenAI-share margin loan shows replacement funding can change collateral; bridge repayment does not by itself establish lower consolidated leverage.

Huachen Energy seeks a second extension, another six years for dollar and yuan bonds, starting at 6% interest and rising 0.5 percentage point annually to 8.5% in year six. Paying a specified principal portion could reduce interest, but annual amortization remains contested. The prior court-approved deal extended five years to December 2026. About $627 million of dollar notes remains; CN¥2 billion onshore refers to the 2021 restructuring, not a current total. CICC advises on the dollar talks.

LIV Golf's bankruptcy brought a different new commitment: Saudi PIF, after withdrawing earlier financing, agreed $49.6 million of debtor-in-possession funding following Tuesday's filing. It finances the process without restoring the old model or determining existing recoveries.

## Inflation and the first expanded buyback provide the next evidence

September 10 PPI is forecast at +0.4% headline and +0.3% core monthly; claims at 205,000 after 206,000. September 11 CPI consensus is +0.4%, core +0.2%, and annual core easing to 2.4% from 2.5%. Non-energy acceleration favors September 16 Fed action; moderation would give mortgage restraint more weight. ECB guidance September 10 will test the roughly 90 basis points priced through end-2027, beyond the expected first hike.

September 10 brings the actual buyback against a $6 billion maximum alongside the 30-year auction. Accepted amounts and liquidity will show whether support contains selling after Wednesday's strong 10-year bidding. Continuing pressure despite good absorption would put more focus on mortgage and options hedges. SoftBank's announced September 15 bridge repayment provides a separate cash-delivery check.

The BOJ's September 18 decision already has a quarter-point increase priced. Subsequent guidance now carries more weight for the yen: slower-than-expected follow-through could reverse appreciation, stronger confirmation could accelerate funding-position adjustments, even while a stronger currency relieves imported inflation.

section_summaries.section_title: Treasuries fall as $6 billion buyback plan disappoints
section_summaries.summary: Oil and a smaller-than-hoped buyback lifted yields despite good auction demand. Credit placement stayed strong, but repeated long exposure met more selective buyers.

section_summaries.section_title: High auction yields attract buyers after buyback expectations unwind
section_summaries.summary: The buyback is a face ceiling, not completed cash spending. The auction cleared well at a high yield, while mortgage extension and options hedging added possible selling pressure.

section_summaries.section_title: Diesel costs extend the inflation problem beyond crude
section_summaries.summary: Diesel cracks reflected lost refining and product exports. European hike pricing extended, but national inflation and growth paths left sharply different room for policy.

section_summaries.section_title: Dell, Amazon and Uber complete large sales with different demand
section_summaries.summary: Dell's growth supported an enlarged sale. Amazon and Uber completed new currencies with differing demand, while MercadoLibre and acquisition borrowers added supply.

section_summaries.section_title: Yen strength encourages alternative funding and offshore yuan access
section_summaries.summary: Yen gains challenged funded positions and encouraged yuan alternatives. Possible pension access and new ECB collateral treatment could change future demand and borrowing capacity.

section_summaries.section_title: Pemex support falls as Dangote repays and SoftBank replaces its bridge
section_summaries.summary: Pemex faces lower proposed aid, Dangote has already repaid debt, and SoftBank is replacing its bridge. Huachen extensions and LIV's bankruptcy funding remain different creditor outcomes.

section_summaries.section_title: Inflation and the first expanded buyback provide the next evidence
section_summaries.summary: Inflation, actual buyback acceptance and the long auction test rates. SoftBank's payment and BOJ follow-through provide separate cash and funding-position checks.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries fall after $6 billion buyback plan falls short of hopes
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasury's $6 billion limit tripled the original plan but missed expectations as high as $10 billion. Long-end selling followed; a $39 billion 10-year reopening at 4.834% cleared through the market and recovered part of the loss.

Diesel premiums widened as refining and product exports suffered, extending pressure beyond crude. Mortgage refinancing weakened, while mortgage and options hedging could amplify further yield gains.

Dell upsized strongly; Amazon's sterling and Uber's euro debuts completed, but order retention and longest-maturity demand differed. SoftBank announced a bridge takeout, Dangote reported actual debt reduction, and Pemex's reduced support depended on operating improvement.
overall_summary.summary: The 10-year closed 3 basis points higher at 4.83%, the 2-year rose 4 to 4.43% and the 30-year 3 to 5.28%. Real yields led the 10-year move as breakevens held at 2.37%.
